Free AAs and Peptide- (or protein)-bound AAs
Free AAs are those AAs that are not covalently bound in dipeptides, oligopeptides, or polypeptides. Aspartate, glutamate, glutamine,
and taurine are among the most predominant free AAs in human tissues (Adibi and Mercer, 1973; Ahlman et al., 1993; Barle et al.,
1996; Perry et al., 1971). In healthy humans, glutamine is the most abundant free AA in their plasma and skeletal muscle, and is the
